definition.description: When an inbound interactive response arrives by reference instead of inline, download and decrypt the referenced attachment and POST the encoded data to https://mspgw.push.apple.com/v1/decodePayload to recover the original interactiveData dictionary the user's device sent.
definition.key_considerations: Apple-hosted POST. Triggered by interactiveDataRef when a payload exceeds roughly 10 KB, which is routine for list picker, form and App Extension responses. items.section: Section B. Core API transport layer

definition.requirement: Implement /authenticate for the OAuth 2.0 Authentication message
definition.description: Send POST https://mspgw.push.apple.com/v1/authenticate with the authentication message body: version 2.0, requestIdentifier, and oauth2 with responseType code, scope, state and redirectURI. The device opens the brand's OAuth URL, and the user signs in on the brand's identity provider. The identity provider redirects to the brand's redirectURI with an authorization code. The brand's back end exchanges the code at its Token URL using the client secret and keeps the tokens on its side. The callback finishes with a 302 to messages-auth://?status=success, failure, cancel or unknown. Apple then sends a webhook to /message carrying requestIdentifier and status, never a token.
definition.key_considerations: Apple hosted POST, used with C.10 and the per brand OAuth config in C.25: OAuth URL and Client Identifier in Apple Business Register, Token URL and client secret in channel settings. Only responseType code is supported. PKCE is not supported. state comes back unmodified. requestIdentifier is not present at the callback, so correlate on state. The EV certificate applies to the redirectURI host. Generate a new requestIdentifier per request and never reuse it; several requests are allowed. One shot: nothing from the sign in travels with later messages, and any session is the brand's own record keyed on the Opaque ID. responseEncryptionKey belongs to the original authenticate flow, deprecated since February 2023
definition.reference:
Chapter 7: API Endpoints Reference
 Chapter 20 > 20.2 Initiating the Flow
MSP Integration Guide §17, §17.2, §17.9, §17.10

items.section: Section B. Core API transport layer

definition.requirement: Honour the Opaque ID identity model
definition.description: sourceId and destinationId on organic AMB are opaque tokens issued by Apple. Never treat them as, transform them into, or persist them alongside, real-world identifiers (phone, email, customer ID) outside of an authenticated linkage.

definition.requirement: Apple Pay Message
definition.description: Send Apple Pay payment requests with merchant session handoff, ApplePayPaymentRequest payload, line items, and shipping methods. Refunds are out of scope for the Apple Pay message: they run in a workflow outside Messages for Business (Apple source: AMB canonical v7.0 L5095). Apple Pay requires the Merchant ID registered on the AMB account before sending a request
definition.key_considerations:
For testing, MSP must have a brand that holds its own Apple Developer account and Apple Pay Merchant ID, not the third-party payment processor's. Payment Processing Certificate enrolment is multi-day. Refunds are handled in a workflow outside Messages for Business. Refund handling is not an in-band AMB feature and is not required within the Apple Pay message
 
 The brand (merchant) owns the Apple Developer account and Apple Pay Merchant ID and shares the Payment Processing Certificate with the MSP. The MSP does not need to hold the processor's enrolments.
 
 Role split: Apple tokenizes the card and issues the merchant session; the MSP transports and authenticates the messages and routes them to the configured endpoints; the brand's own payment gateway and PSP process the charge. Apple Pay in AMB is the presentment and tokenization layer, not the processor. 
 
 Prerequisites: Apple Developer account and Apple Pay Merchant ID configured
 Merchant ID must be on the AMB account first.

Two certificates, two roles: the Merchant Identity Certificate authenticates the merchant session request, and the Payment Processing Certificate lets the payment be processed (Apple source: AMB canonical v7.0 L5147, L5149 to L5173). Which party holds each depends on who requests the merchant session and who decrypts the token; record it per brand in the channel settings (C.25).
definition.reference: Chapter 18: Apple Pay (18.1–18.4)

definition.requirement: Device Capabilities
definition.description: Parse the per-device capability-list on every inbound and provide alternate handling for unsupported features.
definition.key_considerations:
capability-list is per device, not per user. Keep the latest value per conversation, keyed by the customer's opaque ID, and refresh it on every inbound, because the customer can switch devices. The opaque ID is sourceId on an inbound message and destinationId on the MSP's reply; the inbound destinationId is the business ID (Apple source: AMB canonical v7.0 L309, L331). Invitations differ: destinationId is the customer's phone number and no opaque ID exists when the Invitation is sent (Apple source: AMB canonical v7.0 L3930), so there is no conversation whose capability-list could apply; Invitation eligibility follows C.23, not a cached capability-list. Drives Form Message gating and any future feature behind a capability flag.
 
 Apple feedback 2026 08 25: capture device locale alongside the capability list at entry and keep both with the conversation, keyed by the customer's opaque ID as above. Locale drives language selection and localized template choice; capability drives element gating.

items.section: Section F. Human escalation under live-agent. Some applicable if a live-agent is not available at all times or is limited and has been approved by Apple. Default deployments must provide a live human agent during business hours.

definition.requirement: Detect escalation intent
definition.description:
The bot or its NLU layer must classify both trigger words (AGENT, REPRESENTATIVE, HELP) and free-text intent signalling that the user wants a human (e.g. 'talk to a person', 'this isn't helping').
 Note: A quick reply following unrecognized intent is recommended with "Talk to a Human, Callback, email or Send us a Message", see F.2
definition.key_considerations:
Trigger word matching is deterministic; free-text intent uses the bot's NLU. False negatives are worse than false positives here; err toward escalation.
 Note: This is about intent detection 
 Note: Ensure human available hours are expressed when user selects to talk to an agent (E.1), check also E.6
definition.reference:
Chapter 26 > 26.4 Trigger Words (agent / support / help)
 Chapter 26 > 26.1 Live Agent Requirement (actionable keywords, free-text intent handling)

items.section: Section F. Human escalation under live-agent. Some applicable if a live-agent is not available at all times or is limited and has been approved by Apple. Default deployments must provide a live human agent during business hours.

definition.requirement: Present a callback or email choice
definition.description:
On escalation, present the user with a structured choice between a callback request and an email reply (collected via Form Message).
 If the user decides to send a message, the human agent can reply saying the message was acknowledged and a response will be given the next business day if the message was sent out of business hours. Then the human agent will reply to that message in the channel
definition.key_considerations:
This is especially relevant if there is no human support available over messages: the user is presented with alternative options like a call, or sending an email over the channel (messages) with the goal of receiving a response in the channel back from the email response from the human on the other side.
 Use Quick Reply for the binary choice; collect the supporting details (phone number, email, message) via Form Message with fallback to List Picker or plain text on older devices. The in channel handoff must be as seamless as possible; where a live agent is not available, the bot assists the user in composing and sending an email to the brand from within the conversation.
 Note, this is about options presented. 
 Email can be optional if no 7x24 is present and email can be created on the channel and ideally received as a message back when agent is available
definition.reference: Not covered in Integration Guide — the structured callback/email choice is MSP escalation design; only the general escalation duty is specified (26.1).

definition.description: For escalations received outside business hours, allow the user to message the human agents and queue the message to be replied to when the agent is back; also queue the callback for the next business day and queue the email-via-form for review the next business day. State the timing explicitly in the thread.

Chapter 2 > 2.4 The Experience Review (out-of-hours automated message requirement)

definition.requirement: Screen recording, three dimensions
definition.description: Record three end to end flows: bot flow (entry point through resolution or escalation), agent flow (entry point through agent resolution), and a capability flow that shows the same use case on a device that supports the feature and on a device that does not, demonstrating the fallback to Quick Reply, List Picker, Time Picker, or plain text in place of Form Message.
definition.key_considerations: Each recording must include the entry point and a Leave Conversation. Each must be one continuous take, not edited.
definition.reference: Chapter 2 > 2.4 The Experience Review (three review dimensions; What the Recording Must Demonstrate)

items.section: Section G. Integration Review submission pack

definition.requirement: Recording production method
definition.description: Use Apple-recommended recording methods (QuickTime mirroring from iOS, or direct iOS screen recording). Native resolution. No edits. Timestamps documented.
definition.key_considerations:
Edited recordings are rejected. If two takes are needed, submit the second take in full, not a stitched composite. Ensure it is QuickTime, to demonstrate e.g. an Apple Pay full integration on screen.
 Note: Not using QuickTime will prevent seeing an Apple Pay payment interaction on screen, for example
definition.reference: Not covered in Integration Guide — recording production method (QuickTime mirroring, native resolution, no edits) lives in the Onboarding docs.

definition.requirement: Submit and iterate
definition.description: Submit the video pack to Messaging Advisory. Expect at least one iteration cycle with MADV and then with the regional AMB team. Maybe two.
definition.key_considerations: Plan for the iteration. Allocate calendar time for review responses; reviewers usually return comments within a defined SLA but the back-and-forth can span weeks.

Chapter 2 > 2.4 The Experience Review (1–3 review rounds; resubmission with change summary)

items.section: Section H. Response codes, retry, timeouts

definition.requirement: Response code taxonomy
definition.description: Implement and respect the response code taxonomy: 2xx success, 4xx client errors (including 410 Gone with two distinct semantics on organic AMB vs Invitations), and 5xx server errors with a documented retry policy.
definition.key_considerations:
Only 5xx is retried; every 4xx is final for that message (Apple source: AMB canonical v7.0 L397).
 The published /message codes are 200, 400, 401, 403, 404, 410, 500; Apple documents no 429 for AMB, so any rate-limit handling is an MSP-side inference (see DR-15). On organic AMB, 410 means the user closed the conversation; 'no longer reachable' is 404. On Invitations, 410 means a missing or incorrect message-type header. Treat these as distinct states in the MSP data model
definition.reference:
Chapter 24: Response Codes and Error Handling (incl. 404 fallback expectation, 24.1 Retry Logic, 24.2 Handling 410)
 Chapter 22 > 22.7 Response Codes for Invitation Messages

definition.description: Maintain a matrix of timeouts and TTLs by message type and flow stage: typing indicator 60 seconds, Apple Pay merchant session per the session's expires At value (Apple publishes no fixed duration; do not hardcode 5 minutes)., attachment URL TTLs, ratchet between Apple, MSP, and CDN.

items.section: Section H. Response codes, retry, timeouts

definition.requirement: Reliable, ordered, signed and revocable partner webhook delivery
definition.description: Partner webhook events are created atomically with the business transaction and delivered under a documented at-least-once contract; each event carries a stable webhook-id, timestamp and verifiable Standard Webhooks signature; deliveries preserve per-conversation ordering, retry under a bounded policy, resist concurrent/stale workers via leases and fencing, support consumer dedup on webhook-id, and stop after endpoint deactivation.
definition.key_considerations: At least once, not exactly once. Outbox atomic with the journal/state transition; webhook-id stable across retries; sign the exact raw body; document timestamp tolerance + secret rotation; only documented 2xx acks; document retryable responses/timeout/max attempts/terminal state; ordering within a conversation while unrelated conversations progress; deactivation prevents queued events from being claimed or sent; observable attempt/next-retry/last-status/terminal. MSP-platform reliability control; Apple context analogous only.
definition.reference: Not covered in Integration Guide — partner-webhook delivery is a platform (team-lane) contract, not Apple protocol.

items.section: Section H. Response codes, retry, timeouts

definition.requirement: Provisional tracking and safe handling of the reported 365-day reachability window
definition.description: Track the last qualifying inbound per conversation and surface approaching or observed expiry internally to authorized brand operators. The reported 365-day duration is provisional until direct authority is resolved. A qualifying inbound may reset the window, but MUST NOT reset opt-out or campaign consent.
definition.key_considerations: Do not invent an Apple error code, hard-code an unverified duration, or use the timer to authorize outbound. No arbitrary pre-expiry re-engagement is allowed. Outreach is permitted only through an approved, consented Invitation or another channel with independent consent. Define qualifying events, clock skew, and precedence of consent/close over reachability.
definition.reference: Not covered in Integration Guide — the 365-day reachability window is provisional and does not appear in the guide (not even in Chapter 29).

items.section: Section I. Security, privacy, constraints

definition.requirement: Opaque ID handling
definition.description: sourceId and destinationId are opaque tokens. Never persist them alongside personal identifiers outside of an authenticated linkage. Never use them as join keys against PII tables.
definition.key_considerations: Stable per user-brand pair, not reversible. Account linking is via the channel settings landing page, not via id parsing. Logging fields and analytics pipelines must respect this.
definition.reference:
Chapter 27 > 27.1 The Opaque ID
 Chapter 29: Unresolved Gaps (Opaque ID technical spec: behavioural envelope confirmed, internals unpublished)

items.section: Section I. Security, privacy, constraints

definition.requirement: Encryption posture
definition.description: TLS 1.2 or later for all in-transit traffic. Messaging API secret stored in a secrets manager, never in source, logs, or environment files committed to a repository.
definition.key_considerations: Apply standard secret hygiene: rotation policy, access auditing, environment separation. Treat AMB credentials with the same posture as production payment credentials.
definition.reference:
Chapter 27 > 27.2 Encryption Model (TLS; SOC 2 / HIPAA notes)
 Chapter 3 > 3.3 Key Management (secret in a secrets manager)

items.section: Section I. Security, privacy, constraints

definition.requirement: Attachment crypto
definition.description: Implement AES-CTR per-attachment encryption with the key carried in the message body, not in HTTP headers. Decrypt inbound attachments on receipt; encrypt outbound before /preUpload.
definition.key_considerations: Use the self-test vectors in the spec to verify the crypto end to end. Bugs here typically only show up on a specific file size or content type and are easy to miss without targeted tests.
definition.reference:
Chapter 10 > 10.3 Uploading Attachments (Outbound)
 Chapter 10 > 10.4 Downloading Attachments (Inbound)

items.section: Section I. Security, privacy, constraints

definition.requirement: Message history not stored at Apple
definition.description: Apple does not retain conversation history. The MSP is the system of record. Reflect this in brand-facing documentation and in any data-retention or compliance statements.
definition.key_considerations: Apple's privacy posture is that the conversation lives on the user's device and on the MSP's systems, not on Apple's. The brand and MSP own retention policy. Note specifically that any administrative-access requirement (e.g. FERPA in education, or other regulated-sector administrator-access regimes) is the MSP's and brand's responsibility to satisfy, not Apple's.
definition.reference: Chapter 27 > 27.3 Message History

items.section: Section I. Security, privacy, constraints

definition.requirement: Payload size constraints
definition.description: Inline interactiveData above 10 KB is replaced by interactiveDataRef, fetched and decoded through /decodePayload. Each attachment must be smaller than 100 MB (Apple source: AMB canonical v7.0 L1047). The guide publishes no hard limit on the text message body.
definition.key_considerations: 10 KB is the size at which Apple sends interactiveDataRef instead of inline interactiveData (for example most List Picker replies with images), not a cap on what the MSP sends; when an outbound interactive JSON is over 10 KB, Apple's 200 response carries asset references for reuse (Apple source: AMB canonical v7.0 L580, L995, L1813). The 100 MB attachment ceiling is hard (a file must be smaller than 100 MB); for larger files use an external delivery surface linked through a rich link. Any platform limit on the text body or on inflated inbound bodies is a configured default, not Apple's.
definition.reference:
Chapter 28 > 28.1 Payload and Size Limits
 Chapter 6 > 6.2 Handling interactiveDataRef (Payloads Over 10 KB)

items.section: Section I. Security, privacy, constraints

definition.requirement: Partner delivery tenant isolation and secure destination handling
definition.description: Every partner webhook endpoint, subscription, outbox event, retry and delivery is owned by exactly one brand; events are never delivered to, queried by, or replayed through another brand's endpoint. The same isolation applies to the SSE firehose and journal-read APIs. Production destinations use HTTPS and are protected against SSRF, DNS rebinding and unsafe redirects. Apple attachment URLs, keys and signatures are not exposed in partner payloads.
definition.key_considerations: Persist non-null brand_id on webhook endpoints and outbox; derive the event brand in the same transaction that writes the outbox row; never take brand from a partner-controlled field; filter endpoint selection, claims, retries, replay and admin reads by brand; RLS backstops both tables. Signing authenticates a payload, it does not establish tenant isolation. Journal/log secret-minimization is broader than webhooks (coordinate with I.3). MSP-platform security control; not Apple-gated.
definition.reference: Not covered in Integration Guide — tenant isolation for partner webhook delivery is a platform rule, not Apple protocol.

items.section: Section K. MSP omnichannel controls (not Apple protocol requirements)

definition.requirement: Configurable fallback to registered RCS, SMS, or both when the destination is not an Apple device
definition.description: When the intended recipient does not use an Apple device and therefore cannot receive an Apple Messages for Business Invitation or conversation, the MSP may use the brand's registered RCS channel, SMS channel, or both only when each selected channel has its own valid consent and the content can be represented safely. Apple recommends having fallback capability but expresses no preference for RCS, SMS, or their order.
definition.key_considerations: This is destination/channel fallback, not Section D Apple device-feature capability fallback and not a retry of an Apple payload. Never use it to bypass decline, opt-out, Leave Conversation, close, or user-preference suppression. Never carry Apple-specific Authentication, Apple Pay, Form, attachment keys/URLs, or secure PII flows to another channel. If both RCS and SMS are configured, define order, wait time, promotion, late-success deduplication, per-channel audit, and opt-out precedence.
definition.reference: Not covered in Integration Guide — RCS/SMS fallback is an MSP omnichannel control outside the Apple protocol (the guide mentions RCS only descriptively).
